sections.title: Representing a Country
sections.content: In MUN, you do not represent yourself — you represent an assigned country. This means advocating for positions that may differ from your personal beliefs. This is the core skill of diplomatic roleplay.
bullets: Your personal opinion does not matter — your country's policy does
Research your country's actual UN voting record and foreign policy
You must argue positions you may personally disagree with

sections.title: Separating Persona from Bias
sections.content: The ability to separate your identity from your country persona is what distinguishes excellent delegates. It requires research, empathy, and intellectual discipline.
bullets: Understand WHY your country holds its position — history, economics, security
Use the third person: 'My country believes...' not 'I think...'
A good delegate can argue any position persuasively

sections.title: Persona in Action
sections.content: You personally support strong climate action. Your assigned country is a major oil producer that opposes emission caps.
sections.good: 'My country recognizes the importance of economic development for our population. We propose a phased transition that protects livelihoods while addressing environmental concerns.'
sections.bad: 'I personally think we need to reduce emissions, but my country says no.'
sections.explanation: The good response advocates the country's position constructively. The bad response reveals personal bias and undermines the country's stance.

sections.instruction: If your assigned country opposes a treaty you personally support, how must you act?
options: Express your personal support during speeches
Represent the country's position faithfully while working within its policy to find solutions
Ask the chair to reassign your country
sections.feedback: Your duty is to represent your country's position. Find creative solutions within your policy constraints.

sections.q: Why is it important to use 'My country believes' instead of 'I think' in MUN?
options: It reinforces that you are representing a national position, not your personal view
It is required by the rules of procedure
sections.explain: Using 'my country' language maintains the diplomatic roleplay and reminds everyone that you represent a nation.

sections.statement: Good MUN delegates only accept committee assignments for countries whose policies they personally agree with.
sections.feedback: The best delegates can represent any country. The skill is understanding and advocating for positions, not agreeing with them.

sections.sentence: Separating your personal views from your assigned country's position is called maintaining your {0}.
sections.instruction: Fill in the term for staying in character as your assigned country.
sections.feedback: Your persona is the diplomatic character you maintain throughout the conference.

questions.scenario: You are assigned China in a committee on internet freedom. China supports strict internet regulations. You personally believe in free internet access.
questions.question: What is the best approach?
options: Argue for free internet despite your assignment
Research China's position on digital sovereignty and present their policy persuasively
Tell the committee your personal view
questions.feedback: Research and present your country's position professionally. This is the essence of MUN.
